title: Large Language Models in the Abuse Detection Pipeline

bias_targets.methodology: Analyzing toxicity elicitation across thousands of identity groups, stress-testing safety filters, and measuring the over-detection of toxicity (false positives) in benign statements that mention minority groups.
Evaluating synthetic media-bias labels generated by different LLM annotators to identify ideological skews and distinct political leanings.
Conducting targeted adversarial stress tests designed specifically to uncover racism and verify the effectiveness of safety locks for vulnerable racial groups.
Conducting targeted adversarial stress tests designed specifically to uncover antisemitism and verify the effectiveness of safety locks for vulnerable religious groups.
Conducting targeted adversarial stress tests designed specifically to uncover misogyny and verify the effectiveness of safety locks for vulnerable groups.

Comparing the prediction tendencies of instruction-tuned models versus RLHF-aligned models to measure systematic over-refusal (over-predicting abuse) or under-prediction of abusive labels driven by model safety training.
